papers.title: Polar Geometry of Time-Odd EEG Dynamics
papers.summary: The paper introduces a skew-symmetric EEG state-derivative operator K and its spectral counterpart to extract time-odd, subject-discriminative longitudinal EEG features. Across four public datasets, polar orientation improved cross-session subject matching (e.g., Dortmund AUC 0.8901→0.9625, CMC@1 0.4757→0.6214), with fixed alpha-beta fusion reaching CMC@1=0.8350 and AUC=0.9855.

papers.title: Personalised federated learning for Riemannian and Euclidean EEG decoding
papers.summary: This paper introduces personalised federated learning for two lightweight EEG decoders, Riemannian SPDNet and Euclidean EEGNet, where all subjects share a trunk but each keeps an individual head. Personalised SPDNet achieves higher accuracy than standard FL and centralised training, converges in fewer rounds, communicates fewer parameters, and outperforms every EEGNet configuration on two of three motor-imagery datasets.

papers.title: MF-PNet: A Lightweight Multi-Frequency Progressive Neural Network for Depression Classification Deployed on Wearable EEG Sensors.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Introduced MF-PNet, a multi-frequency progressive neural network for depression classification using three-channel wearable EEG, achieving 98.8% accuracy in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on an in-house cohort. The model was compressed to a MobileNetV3 student for embedded deployment, with INT8 quantization maintaining 98.5% accuracy and 45.99 ms inference latency on an MCU.

papers.title: A dual-branch multidimensional attention fusion network for EEG-based fatigue classification.
papers.summary: Introduces DB-MDAFNet, a lightweight dual-branch network combining spectral-temporal and inter-channel dependency features for EEG fatigue classification. Achieves 85.58% accuracy on SEED-VIG and 97.12%-98.56% on a self-constructed dataset with only 0.185M parameters.

papers.title: Non-Markovian Dynamical Systems Modeling of Electroencephalogram-Based Brain Activity for Predicting the Cognitive Fatigue Level.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper develops a fractional dynamical networks-based machine learning framework using coupled fractional-order differential equations to model non-Markovian EEG brain activity and detect cognitive fatigue transitions. It reports distinct multifractal signatures across fatigue levels, with Wasserstein distances of 0.10, 0.13, and 0.08 between states 0-1, 1-2, and 0-2, and achieves 93.33% classification accuracy and 95% AUROC.

papers.title: Img2EEG: A Scalable and Interpretable Encoding Framework for Simulating Human EEG Responses to Visual Inputs.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces Img2EEG, a participant-specific image-to-EEG encoding framework integrating hierarchical visual and semantic representations to generate temporally resolved EEG responses. Trained on THINGS EEG2, it generalized to unseen images, reproduced the face-sensitive N170, and scaled to 1.28 million ImageNet images producing over 12 million synthetic EEG responses that supported cross-dataset visual reconstruction.

papers.title: AERIAL: Adversarial Evaluation of Robustness in Accuracy-Preserving Low-Precision EEG Decoders
papers.summary: This paper evaluates how accuracy-preserving compression affects adversarial robustness of EEG decoders by comparing FP32 EEGNet and ShallowConvNet with global magnitude pruning and simulated INT8 post-training quantization and quantization-aware training on BCI Competition IV-2a. It finds that accuracy-preserving compression does not improve direct robustness, with EEGNet PGD accuracy remaining 22-24% at epsilon=0.005, but pruning reduces bidirectional adversarial transfer efficiency to 0.963/0.928 versus 0.994/0.997 for post-training quantization.

papers.title: ADHD classification using spherical phase space partitioning and symbolic time series analysis of multi-channel EEG signals.
papers.summary: The paper proposes an EEG-based ADHD classification framework combining spherical phase space partitioning with entropy-optimized symbolic time series analysis, followed by cosine similarity and bidirectional LSTM classification. Using 20-second EEG windows from 61 children with ADHD and 60 healthy controls during a visual attention task, it achieves up to 98% classification accuracy.

papers.title: Editorial: Modern applications of EEG in neurological and cognitive research.
papers.summary: This editorial introduces a special issue on modern EEG applications in neurological and cognitive research, highlighting biomarkers, brain-computer interfaces, cognitive neuroscience, machine learning, neurological disorders, and signal processing. As an editorial, it provides no abstract and reports no primary findings.

papers.title: Systematic Benchmarking of a Dry Electrode EEG Prototype Against Wet Electrode EEG Systems in Electrophysiological/Cognitive Scenarios.
papers.summary: A dry electrode EEG system was developed and benchmarked against a commercial wet EEG system in 19 participants across resting-state, SSVEP, and motor imagery tasks. The dry system showed comparable performance to the wet system in power spectral density, SNR, and single-trial classification accuracy (SSVEP: 80.08% vs 81.10%; MI: 72.46% vs 70.7%).

papers.title: Multimodal sensor-based response mechanisms of drivers under adverse weather conditions using EEG spectral entropy and prediction entropy.
papers.summary: Investigates driver-state dynamics under clear, rain, snow, and fog using multimodal sensors and entropy measures. Finds distinct response pathways: rain increases cognitive load, snow synchronizes neural complexity and system uncertainty, and fog induces conservative compensation, with a fusion model achieving 91.9% accuracy.

papers.title: A dynamic multi-branch EEG decoding network for motor imagery classification with preliminary clinical validation.
papers.summary: A dynamic multi-branch EEG decoding network (DMB-EDN) was proposed for motor imagery classification, integrating learnable time-frequency representations, rhythm-specific spectral modeling, and trial-conditioned dynamic fusion. It achieved 96.41% accuracy on BCI Competition IV 2a and 85.00% accuracy on a spinal cord injury dataset under leave-one-subject-out evaluation.

papers.title: Entropy-Based Analysis of Olfactory EEG as a Candidate Biomarker for Early Mild Cognitive Impairment Detection: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study analyzed olfactory-evoked EEG complexity using Multivariate Multiscale Multi-Frequency Entropy (M3FrEn) to discriminate mild cognitive impairment (MCI) patients from healthy subjects. MCI subjects showed significantly reduced stimulus-related entropy modulation in early post-stimulus periods, and a classification accuracy of approximately 92% was achieved.

papers.title: EEG correlates of sleep stages, sleep discrepancy, and insomnia: a comparative analysis of people with insomnia and healthy sleepers using spectral power and sample entropy.
papers.summary: Compares EEG band power and sample entropy across sleep stages, sleep discrepancy, and insomnia status in 64 participants. Finds EEG metrics strongly reflect sleep stages but poorly distinguish self-reported sleep perception and inconsistently differentiate insomnia from controls, with regional differences in delta, beta, and entropy.

papers.title: Normalization accounts for temporal dynamics in human somatosensory cortex.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: Using fMRI and intracranial EEG in humans, the study found that somatosensory cortical responses to vibrotactile stimuli exhibit sub-additive temporal summation, which is better explained by divisive normalization than linear integration. This suggests that normalization is a canonical computation shared with the visual system.

papers.title: Frontal midline theta reduction during attentional reconfiguration links local cortical dynamics to network-level connectivity changes.
papers.summary: The study investigated attentional reconfiguration in 36 healthy adults using a rule-switching 2-back task with EEG. Transient reductions in frontal midline theta (Fmθ) were associated with general network-level theta connectivity increases and local parietal alpha suppression selectively related to spatial processing.

papers.title: Toward precision acupuncture for depression: EEG microstate biomarkers and explainable machine learning for TECAS response.
papers.summary: Developed an explainable machine-learning framework integrating baseline EEG microstate dynamics and clinical features to predict antidepressant response to TECAS in 50 first-episode, drug-naïve MDD patients. The random forest model achieved AUC=0.912, with microstate D duration, coverage, and occurrence as key predictors; responders showed shorter duration, lower coverage, and reduced occurrence of microstate D at baseline.

papers.title: EEG-Based Characterization of Learning Potential-Related Neural Representations via Dynamic Assessment Tasks.
papers.summary: Investigated whether task-evoked EEG responses during a dynamic learning paradigm can characterize individual differences in task-specific learning performance under graduated instructional support in 50 undergraduates. The EEG-based Multi-scale Learning Potential Assessment (MS-LPA) framework, including entropy-based features and functional connectivity matrices with a ResNet-18 model, achieved accuracies of 0.77 and 0.83, respectively, outperforming traditional outcome-driven evaluation.

papers.title: Interictal epileptiform discharges on scalp electroencephalography: Reproducibility of visual interpretation-A systematic review.
papers.summary: Systematic review of reproducibility in visual interpretation of interictal epileptiform discharges on scalp EEG, analyzing 32 studies. Reproducibility varied by clinical context: moderate in unselected populations (kappa ~0.4-0.6), higher in known epilepsy (kappa ~0.8), and lower in acute brain dysfunction (kappa ~0.3-0.5).

papers.title: The Neurophysiology of Cybersickness: A Systematic Review of Neuromarkers, Neurostimulation, and Reporting Practices in Virtual Reality.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics
papers.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 92 studies synthesizing the neurophysiology of visually induced motion sickness in virtual reality, covering EEG, fNIRS, and neurostimulation. The review found that increased low-frequency (delta and theta) power is the most consistent EEG correlate, while alpha-band inconsistencies are partly attributed to VR display type; it also identified recurrent reporting gaps that limit interpretability of classification models.

papers.title: Timing-dependent inhibitory effects of peripheral somatosensory inputs on the primary motor cortex: A transcranial magnetic stimulation-electroencephalography study.
papers.summary: Examined whether subtle differences in afferent timing modulate cortical responses during short-latency afferent inhibition (SAI) using TMS-EEG in 30 healthy adults. Both SAIN20+2 and SAIN20+5 reduced MEP amplitudes, with greater inhibition at SAIN20+2; however, the N45 component of TMS-evoked potentials was specifically modulated only in SAIN20+5, suggesting distinct timing-dependent mechanisms.

papers.title: Self-Concentration Detection Based on Doubled Amplitude/Phase Processing in Node PDE Modular Models.
papers.summary: Proposes a brain-inspired doubled amplitude/frequency signal processing approach within node PDE modular models for self-concentration detection from EEG. Two machine learning methodologies were compared: evolutionary PDE transform and deep learning recurrent processing achieved predictive accuracy above 90% on untrained data when evaluating entire sessions, while regular row-wise modeling reached above 70% accuracy.

papers.title: Voice and linguistic features support early attentional filtering of irrelevant stimuli.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In an EEG study of auditory attention, listeners attended to lateralized target syllables while distractor streams were manipulated for voice and linguistic content. Both acoustic (voice) and linguistic dissimilarity of distractors independently improved early attentional filtering, as reflected by larger target-evoked EEG responses, and recall was poor only when both voice and linguistic content were similar.

papers.title: Multimodal single-cell dataset of juvenile rat neocortical interneurons-Morphology, whole-cell patch electrophysiology and histological slices.
papers.summary: Presents a multimodal single-cell dataset of juvenile rat neocortical interneurons, pairing 3D morphological reconstructions, whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, and histological slide images for 244 cells. The dataset is FAIR-compliant and intended for studying structure-function relationships.

papers.title: A Low-Cost Wearable Multimodal Brain Signal Acquisition System Integrating EEG and fNIRS for Depression Detection.
papers.summary: The study developed a low-cost wearable EEG-fNIRS system using conductive rubber electrodes and validated it through noise, alpha rhythm, SSVEP, and breath-hold experiments. In 31 subjects (15 with depression), the multimodal system detected depression with an accuracy 8.4% higher than EEG alone and 23.5% higher than fNIRS alone.

papers.title: Music as Neuromodulation: A Systematic Review with Insights from Human Intracranial Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized human intracranial electrophysiology studies on music perception, following PRISMA guidelines. It identified robust evidence for basic acoustic feature encoding in auditory cortex and moderate evidence for predictive processing, while proposing music as a neuromodulator that coordinates distributed brain systems.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machine and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states using resting-state EEG features, including spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved the highest performance with 96.88% accuracy at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Multimodal machine learning model integrating electroencephalography, heart rate variability and clinical measures for distinguishing major psychiatric disorders.
papers.summary: The study developed multimodal machine learning models integrating EEG, heart rate variability, and clinical measures to differentiate bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and schizophrenia in 1035 patients. The CatBoost-based multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.776, outperforming unimodal models, with EEG connectivity features in delta, alpha, and gamma bands being important.

papers.title: Cue validity moderates the effects of haptic feedback in simulated instrument flight.
papers.summary: This study examined whether haptic cue validity moderates pilot situational awareness and performance in simulated instrument flight, with eye-tracking and EEG. Haptic cueing improved altitude adherence and increased altimeter fixation, while control participants had better heading adherence and showed higher workload and fatigue and lower engagement on EEG.

papers.title: Neurofeedback as an emerging rehabilitation strategy for Parkinson's disease: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized 18 empirical studies on neurofeedback in Parkinson's disease across EEG-based, fMRI-based, and DBS-guided paradigms. It found that self-regulation of disease-relevant neural signals (sensorimotor rhythms, motor regions, subthalamic beta activity) is feasible in at least some patients, but clinical effects remain heterogeneous and preliminary due to small samples and methodological limits.

papers.title: Neural Responsivity to Unexpected Stimuli Moderates a Developmental Pathway to Anxiety: A Community-Sample Replication in Early Infancy and Childhood.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In 147 infants from a community sample, the mismatch response (MMR) at 4 months moderated developmental pathways from negative reactivity to behavioral inhibition and from behavioral inhibition to childhood anxiety. More negative MMR was associated with risk pathways, and anxiety symptoms were stable from 30 months to 4–6 years.

papers.title: Integrative AI-based multiomic and neurophysiological profiling of chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis: study protocol for the prospective, observational, case-control RA-PAIN-AI study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational case-control study aims to identify clinical, neurophysiological, and multiomic signatures of chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis patients using integrative AI-based analysis. The protocol details recruitment of at least 50 patients per group, with whole genome sequencing, transcriptomics, secretomics, and EEG in an exploratory subset, and prespecified machine-learning validation procedures.

papers.title: Integrated Neurorehabilitation Including EEG-Neurofeedback for Unilateral Spatial Neglect After Right Thalamo-Mesencephalic Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 70-year-old patient with unilateral spatial neglect after right thalamo-mesencephalic hemorrhage who underwent a 3-week multidisciplinary rehabilitation including 15 EEG-neurofeedback sessions. Post-treatment assessments showed improvements in cognition, neglect, and functional independence, but causality cannot be attributed to neurofeedback alone due to concurrent therapies.

papers.title: Seizures in SRRM2-related disorder and treatment response.
papers.journal: European journal of paediatric neurology : EJPN : official journal of the European Paediatric Neurology Society
papers.summary: This retrospective international study characterized the epilepsy phenotype in seven individuals with SRRM2 loss-of-function variants, finding a median seizure onset at 18 months, often initial febrile seizures, and favourable response to antiseizure medications with no drug-resistant cases.

papers.title: Neural Dynamics of Self-Control: Pre-Choice EEG Signals Predict Yielding to Temptation
papers.summary: Introduced a dynamometer-based task in which 26 participants chose between high-effort/larger-later and low-effort/smaller-sooner rewards during 32-channel EEG, producing frequent switching toward smaller-sooner options in temptation trials. Pre-choice late positive potential differentiated stay from switch trials, and multivariate decoding discriminated outcomes 304–348 ms post-option presentation via frontal and centroparietal networks, indicating that neural bias toward yielding is established before the initial choice and reflects reward anticipation rather than self-control signals.

papers.title: Ganoderic Acid A Ameliorates Pentylenetetrazol-Induced Epilepsy in Mice via Activating KCNQ2.
papers.summary: This study investigated the antiepileptic effects of Ganoderic acid A (GA-A) in pentylenetetrazol-induced epileptic mice. GA-A reduced seizure severity, neuronal loss, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress, directly bound to and activated KCNQ2 channels, and its effects on EEG abnormalities and anxiety/depression-like behaviors were weakened by hippocampal KCNQ2 knockout.

papers.title: Multimodal Characterization of Atrial Fibrillation: From Patient-Specific Anatomy and Electrophysiology to Standardized Atrial Mapping.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes a multimodal framework for characterizing atrial fibrillation, integrating patient-specific anatomical reconstruction, electrophysiological profiling, and standardized spatial mapping. It discusses how these integrated data can parameterize computational models for mechanistic insight and personalized management while noting barriers to clinical translation.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Acquisition of balinese imagined spelling using electroencephalogram (BISE) dataset" [Data in Brief, volume 60, June 2025, 111454].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum to the article 'Acquisition of balinese imagined spelling using electroencephalogram (BISE) dataset' published in Data in Brief, and the abstract contains only the correction notice.

papers.title: Synergistic effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and a dance movement intervention on mild cognitive impairment: study protocol for a four-arm factorial randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a four-arm factorial randomized controlled trial to evaluate the synergistic effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and a culturally tailored dance movement intervention on cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, with the primary outcome being global cognition measured by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.

papers.title: Maternal willingness to participate in research involving neuroimaging, biological sample collection, and data storage: Towards a Multicentre Neurodevelopmental Research in a low-resource setting.
papers.summary: This multicentre study surveyed 300 mothers in a low-resource setting to assess willingness to participate in neurodevelopmental research involving neuroimaging, biological sample collection, and long-term data storage. Willingness was high for brain health testing (92%) and routine biospecimens (>95%), but lower for sensitive specimens (16-55%) and 10-year storage (48%), with maternal education, marital status, and income predicting consent.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
